topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the fifth lecture in the series and outlines the learning outcomes concerning cancer evolution, cell of origin, and microenvironmental influences.

topics.label: Clonal selection and epigenetic drivers of tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how sequential genetic mutations confer Darwinian selective fitness and how epigenetic alterations modify transcriptional states to drive tumor initiation and progression.

topics.label: Stem cell properties and cell-of-origin models in tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how stem cell hierarchies relate to cancer development, presenting stochastic versus cancer stem cell models alongside experimental evidence from leukemia and colorectal cancer.

topics.label: Microenvironmental promotion, chronic inflammation, and stromal dependency
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how external promoters, inflammatory signaling, and surrounding stromal tissue provide essential supportive conditions for tumor growth and progression.

topics.label: Experimental and computational tools for analyzing tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic focuses on the laboratory technologies and computational methods used to map mutational timing, cellular plasticity, and microenvironmental interactions in cancer.

topics.label: Integrated multifactorial framework of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes how genetic mutations, cell-of-origin characteristics, transcriptional states, and microenvironmental factors collectively determine diverse evolutionary pathways to malignancy.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview of cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and previews the subsequent lecture on cancer therapy.
